source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter I, §6 General Strategy of the Opening, Example 17

steps.title: The main thing
steps.source: The main thing is to develop the pieces quickly. Get them into play as fast as you can. From the outset two moves, 1 P - K 4 or 1 P - Q 4, open up lines for the Queen and a Bishop.

narration.say: The main thing in the opening is to develop the pieces quickly.
Two first moves, e4 and d4, open lines for the queen and a bishop at once.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Open lines for the queen and the king's bishop.

feedback.d4: Just as good in principle, but this example follows e4.
feedback.e3: That opens lines too, but e4 also takes the centre.
feedback.*: Push the king's pawn two squares.

exercise.hint: The pawn in front of the king goes two squares.

narration.say: Knight to f3: both an attacking and a developing move. It attacks e5.
Knight to c6 develops, and at the same time defends the pawn.
Knight to c3, knight to f6: purely developing moves.

steps.title: Your turn: develop and attack
steps.source: It is generally advisable not to bring this Bishop out until one Knight is out, preferably the King's Knight. The Bishop could also have been played to B 4, but it is advisable whenever possible to combine development and attack.

narration.say: Now a bishop. Whenever possible, combine development with attack.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Develop the king's bishop with an attack.

feedback.Bc4: A good developing move, but b5 also attacks the knight that defends e5.
feedback.*: Develop the bishop so that it attacks something.

exercise.hint: The bishop attacks the knight on c6.
exercise.success: 4. Bb5. Black does the same: Bb4.

steps.title: Castling brings the rook in
steps.source: 5 O - O, an indirect way of preventing 5…B x Kt. […] At the same time the Rook is brought into action in the centre, a very important point.

narration.say: White castles. This indirectly prevents Bxc3, and brings the rook into the centre.
Pawn to d3, pawn to d6: they protect the e-pawns and open the diagonals for the queen's bishops.

steps.title: Your turn: a very powerful move

narration.say: Develop the last minor piece, with a pin.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Develop the queen's bishop with a pin.

feedback.*: The bishop on c1 can pin the knight on f6.

exercise.success: 7. Bg5. A very powerful move: White already threatens Nd5. Black is forced to take on c3.

steps.title: Seven moves of development
steps.source: First, the complete development of the opening has taken only seven moves. […] Third, White by the exchange brings up a Pawn to control the square Q 4, puts Black on the defensive, and thus keeps the initiative.

narration.say: The complete development has taken only seven moves.
White takes back towards the centre. The doubled pawn is no problem this early.
The new pawn controls d4, Black is on the defensive, and White keeps the initiative.

steps.title: Principles of the opening
steps.source: Before development has been completed no piece should be moved more than once, unless it is essential in order to obtain either material advantage or to secure freedom of action.

narration.say: Bring out the knights before the bishops.
And before development is complete, do not move a piece twice, unless you win material or need freedom of action.
